newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet, trade ponders INRO's move.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet, trade ponders INRO's move.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midsession on Thursday with several dealers wondering if the International Natural Rubber Organisation (INRO) will intervene in the market, traders said.
"I think everybody's waiting for some news on how INRO will move in the market. Everybody in the trade is a little curious about that," a trader said.
The five-day moving average was at 185.11 Malaysian/Singapore cents a kg on July 8 while INRO's 'may-buy' level was set at 183.00 cents.
Other dealers said INRO may hold back and only step in if prices slipped to the 'must-buy' level which is about 10 cents lower than their may-buy level.
"I don't know if INRO will really come in on a 'may-buy' basis. I think they may even wait a while to see how things develop," another dealer said.

At around 0445 GMT, September RSS3 was indicated at 90.00-92.00 U.S. cents a kg from 92.00 cents. September RSS1 was indicated at 134.50-136.50 Singapore cents (94-95 U.S. cents) a kg from 136.00 cents.
